item.title: Sean Payton says he hasn't considered benching Bo Nix
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Thursday night's overtime win by the Broncos over the Seahawks, Prime Video's Ryan Fitzpatrick sharply criticized quarterback Bo Nix, calling his performance "garbage."
item.content:encoded:
After Thursday night's overtime win by the Broncos over the Seahawks, Prime Video's Ryan Fitzpatrick sharply criticized quarterback Bo Nix, calling his performance "garbage."

Broncos coach Sean Payton clearly doesn't see it that way.

On Monday, Payton was asked by reporters whether he has considered making a quarterback change.

“To answer your question, no," Payton said. "He’s going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved. The improved play from our offensive line, the more efficient we are relative to balance, running the football. That’s our jobs as coaches here. We talked after the game about we’re excited to get that win, and yet at the same time find that improvement we need in all areas. So, it starts with all of us.”

Payton also was asked whether he listens to any of the media comments about Nix, including Fitzpatrick's remarks.

“I try to focus on the next day here," Payton said. "We’re trying to focus on getting ready to play Arizona. That’s kind of where our attention is.”

Payton could have taken the bait to talk about Fitzpatrick. Payton chose not to do it. If he had chimed in, Payton's response could have been nearly as entertaining as Aqib Talib’s takedown of Fitzpatrick.

Meanwhile, Fitzpatrick will get another chance to evaluate and critique Nix. The Broncos face the Steelers on Black Friday, and the game will be televised by Prime Video.

item.title: For Andy Dalton, the Falcons made the most sense
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sooner rather than later, new Falcons quarterback Andy Dalton will explain his decision to choose the Falcons over the Eagles and other options.
item.content:encoded:
Sooner rather than later, new Falcons quarterback Andy Dalton will explain his decision to choose the Falcons over the Eagles and other options.

And, yes, he had other options beyond the Eagles. But the Falcons made the most sense for Dalton.

For now, Dalton arrives as No. 3 on a four-man depth chart. His decision to take the job in Atlanta suggests that he sees a potential path to becoming No. 2.

Before the season, the possibility of cutting Tua Tagovailoa was on the table. But when starter Michael Penix Jr. was not yet ready to play and an oblique injury to Tua three days before the season opener gave Cooper Rush two opportunities to show what he can do, the Falcons knew Rush couldn't be the primary backup.

Dalton now has the chance to earn the spot that Tua holds. And Dalton's presence gives the Falcons a seasoned veteran who will embrace the task of helping Penix fully develop. That's not to say Tua isn't trying to mentor Penix, but Dalton has played much more football than Tua.

Still, the quickest path to Dalton playing could be in Atlanta. Penix, who suffered a rib injury late in the Week 5 loss to the Ravens and who was back in the medical tent briefly on Sunday against the Bears, has lingering durability issues. If/when Dalton surpasses Tua and if/when Penix is injured, Dalton will be on the field, with a healthy complement of weapons in Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts.

Of course, Dalton could have ended up playing for the Eagles, who cut him due to the roster-management realities of keeping retired right tackle Lane Johnson on the team until June 2027, for cap purposes. Although Tanner McKee had moved past Dalton into the No. 2 spot in Philly, injury to or prolonged ineffectiveness from McKee would have given Dalton a shot.

Both teams, with identical records of 2-4, remain very much alive in divisions that lack powerhouse franchises. The Panthers lead the NFC South at 3-2, and the Giants top the NFC East at 3-2-1.
